questions.question: Which finding is most concerning for impending pediatric respiratory failure?
choices: A lower respiratory rate accompanied by exhaustion and reduced air movement
questions.explanation: A tiring child may lose the ability to sustain tachypnea. Falling effort with exhaustion, altered status, or poor air movement can signal impending failure.

questions.question: A seven-month-old has a typical mild bronchiolitis presentation. Which plan best matches AAP guidance?
choices: Support nasal clearance, hydration, oxygenation assessment, and follow-up without routine imaging or medications
Order routine chest radiography and antibiotics
Give systemic steroids to every infant
Schedule daily albuterol regardless of response
questions.explanation: Typical bronchiolitis is diagnosed clinically and treated supportively; routine imaging, albuterol, epinephrine, steroids, and antibiotics are not recommended.

questions.question: Which croup finding most increases urgency?
questions.explanation: Stridor at rest and retractions indicate clinically important upper-airway obstruction requiring prompt treatment and observation or escalation.

questions.question: A child suddenly coughs while eating and develops unilateral wheeze. What is the priority diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Abrupt onset during eating with unilateral findings strongly suggests an aspirated foreign body, which requires urgent evaluation even if imaging is normal.

questions.question: Why can a quiet chest be dangerous during a severe asthma exacerbation?
choices: Critically reduced airflow may produce little audible wheeze
It proves the asthma has resolved
questions.explanation: Minimal airflow through severely narrowed airways may reduce wheeze; a quiet chest with distress or fatigue can indicate life-threatening obstruction.

questions.question: Which feature makes pneumonia more likely than uncomplicated viral upper-respiratory infection?
choices: Fever with tachypnea, hypoxemia, and focal crackles
questions.explanation: Fever plus tachypnea, hypoxemia, or focal lung findings raises the probability of pneumonia and may change testing, treatment, and disposition.

questions.question: A young infant with cough develops apnea and cyanosis. Which action is safest?
questions.explanation: Apnea and cyanosis in a young infant are emergency findings and may accompany pertussis, bronchiolitis, sepsis, or other serious disease.

questions.question: What is the best role for chest radiography in pediatric respiratory illness?
choices: Use it when uncertainty, hypoxemia, significant distress, complication, foreign body, or treatment failure may change care
Use it only to decide whether a virus is present
questions.explanation: Imaging is most useful when it addresses a specific management-changing question; routine films in typical bronchiolitis can cause overdiagnosis and unnecessary antibiotics.

questions.question: Why must hydration be assessed in a child with respiratory disease?
choices: Tachypnea and fatigue can reduce intake, and severe work of breathing may make feeding unsafe
Every respiratory illness requires IV fluid
Urine output is unrelated to respiratory care
questions.explanation: Respiratory effort, fever, and nasal obstruction can impair intake; inability to hydrate safely is an important reason to escalate care.

questions.question: Which outpatient respiratory plan is safest?
choices: Discharge any child with a normal temperature
Rely only on the oxygen saturation
Provide diagnosis-specific care plus hydration goals, medication technique, follow-up, and explicit emergency signs
questions.explanation: Safe outpatient care depends on stable physiology, adequate intake, an appropriate treatment plan, caregiver ability, reassessment, and clear return precautions.
